title: Keep each wagon at least as cohesive internally as coupled to any single neighbor wagon (advisory)

facts.note: Scope gate: the rule concerns the wagon/WMBT plan corpus. Composition: file_kind scopes the rule; EITHER the operation fact (an authoring edit) OR a corpus-wide assessment of existing eligible wagons triggers it. Neither an edit nor an already-emitted finding is required to assess an existing wagon.
Alternative trigger (not a required gate): adding, moving or editing WMBTs (incl. object_of_control) or wagons changes the shared-token graph.

Alternative trigger (not a required gate): the separability validator builds the WMBT shared-token graph over the whole corpus and compares cohesion vs max single-neighbor coupling for every wagon meeting the min-graph-size guard.

fires: A wagon meeting the min-graph-size guard has, on the single WMBT shared-token graph (edges = WMBT pairs sharing >= min_shared salient object_of_control tokens), fewer intra-wagon edges than the qualifying cross-wagon edges to some single neighbor wagon.
A corpus-wide separability assessment of existing wagons (no edit in progress) finds such a wagon and emits an advisory [MERGE] finding.
doesNotFire: A wagon with fewer WMBTs than the configured min-graph-size guard (skipped, not flagged).
A wagon whose intra-wagon edge count is greater than or equal to its cross-wagon edge count with every single neighbor wagon (equality is separable).
Edits to code or tests that do not change wagons, WMBTs or their object_of_control.

given: A wagon (at or above the min-graph-size guard) whose WMBTs, connected when they share >= min_shared salient object_of_control tokens, form one undirected graph with neighboring wagons' WMBTs
when: You author or revise the wagon's WMBTs, allocate WMBTs across wagons, or review existing wagons
then: Plan the wagon so its cohesion (intra-wagon WMBT edges) is >= its coupling (cross-wagon edges) to every single neighbor wagon; otherwise expect an advisory [MERGE] signal.
prefer: When a wagon is more bound to one neighbor than to itself, treat the [MERGE] signal as an advisory hint to consider merging it with that neighbor.
Judge cohesion and coupling on the same WMBT shared-token graph so the two counts are commensurable.
avoid: Treating a [MERGE] finding as blocking or gating the plan — it is advisory only and never blocks.
Flagging wagons below the min-graph-size guard on account of separability.
Rewording object_of_control tokens merely to dodge shared-token edges instead of reconsidering the wagon boundary.
unless: The wagon is below the configured min-graph-size guard: it is skipped, not flagged.
why: A wagon should be a separable unit of work; if it is more bound to one neighbor than to itself, its boundary may be wrong, so the advisory signal suggests considering a merge with its tightest neighbor.
evidence: Separability validator output shows no [MERGE] advisory for the wagon, or the wagon is reported as skipped by the min-graph-size guard.
For a flagged wagon: cohesion(W) and max over neighbors N of coupling(W,N) counts from the single WMBT shared-token graph.
verifier_detail: Build ONE undirected graph over all WMBTs; an edge joins two WMBTs that share >= min_shared salient tokens taken from object_of_control.
cohesion(W) = number of intra-wagon edges; coupling(W,N) = number of cross-wagon edges between W and neighbor N.

Separable iff cohesion(W) >= max over neighbors N of coupling(W,N) (term 'separable': cohesion(W) >= max-neighbor coupling(W,N) on the WMBT shared-token graph). Non-separable wagons emit an ADVISORY [MERGE] finding — more coupled to a neighbor than cohesive internally (term 'merge_signal': a wagon whose tightest single-neighbor coupling exceeds its internal cohesion — advisory hint to merge).
Cohesion and coupling must be measured on the same WMBT shared-token graph (commensurable).
Wagons below the min-graph-size guard are skipped, not flagged.
Token vocabulary, min_shared and min-graph-size are config-driven calibration knobs under planner.wagon.*; promotion to strict is deferred to calibration.
